result.summary: This is a typical urban residential street with continuous sidewalks and parallel parking on both sides. While sidewalks are present, they are narrow and obstructed by utility poles, and there are no marked pedestrian crossings visible along this stretch of the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective walking width and accessibility.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sidewalks along the block

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates a visual barrier between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge areas visible, forcing pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic and parking without designated protection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Mid-Block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a legal and safer crossing point for residents.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees in the furniture zone to provide a physical buffer, improve the pedestrian environment, and naturally encourage slower driving speeds.

result.summary: The image depicts a two-lane urban street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossing infrastructure. A pedestrian is observed crossing mid-block, which is hazardous due to the absence of signage, markings, or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Unmarked Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: A pedestrian is crossing the street where there are no markings or signs to alert drivers, creating a high risk of collision.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching motorists until they are already in the travel lane.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a continental-style marked crosswalk to clearly define the pedestrian path and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Yield to Pedestrian' signs to reinforce the right-of-way at the crossing point.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane roadway with parallel on-street parking. While the walkways are in good condition, the environment lacks mid-block crossings and traffic calming, with parked vehicles creating potential sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, including a large service van, block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of protected crossings
hazards.description: The absence of mid-block crossings or curb extensions forces pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without designated protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway between intersections.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a marked crosswalk with high-visibility striping and signage to provide a designated and safer crossing point.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and traffic, which also helps to naturally slow vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses and an exceptionally wide concrete sidewalk. While the walkway is clear and continuous, there is a complete lack of physical buffering, such as trees or street furniture, between pedestrians and the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or vertical element (like trees or bollards) between the wide sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install a row of street trees or a landscaped buffer to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.description: If this block leads to an intersection, curb extensions should be added to narrow the roadway and improve visibility.
